title: Errors, tests and explicit input contracts
outcome: Validate scientific inputs, test expected failures and preserve unexpected errors instead of turning them into successful results.

exercises.title: Keep valid zero
exercises.expected: The result is the valid number 0.
exercises.hint: Do not confuse a zero result with rejection.
exercises.answer: The input satisfies the contract and its arithmetic mean happens to be zero.

exercises.title: Reject empty input
exercises.task: Call the helper on an empty vector.
exercises.expected: ArgumentError identifies the missing observation requirement.
exercises.answer: A fabricated zero would hide the absence of evidence.

exercises.title: Reject nonfinite values
exercises.task: Include NaN or Inf in the input.
exercises.hint: Check the numeric domain before aggregation.
exercises.answer: Nonfinite values need a declared policy rather than silent propagation into a report.

exercises.title: Preserve an unexpected error
exercises.task: Pass a value for which the required methods do not exist.
exercises.expected: The unexpected method error is rethrown.
exercises.hint: Catch only the failures that the boundary promises to handle.
exercises.answer: A broad catch can hide a programming defect behind a normal-looking outcome.

exercises.title: Test independently
exercises.task: Validate a result using a hand calculation and a limiting case.
exercises.expected: The assertion has an independent basis.
exercises.hint: Avoid copying the same implementation expression.
exercises.answer: Different reasoning paths reduce the chance that code and test share one unnoticed error.

exercises.title: Report rejected rows
exercises.task: Aggregate valid outcomes from a mixed input stream.
exercises.expected: Retain counts and reasons for rejected rows.
exercises.answer: Selection through validation can change the target population and should remain visible.
